name: Azure Databricks
oneLiner: First-party lakehouse platform — managed Spark, Delta Lake and ML on Azure.
whatItIs: Azure Databricks is the Databricks lakehouse platform delivered as a first-party Azure service — jointly engineered with Microsoft, sold and billed through Azure, and deeply integrated with Entra ID, ADLS, Synapse and Power BI. Like Databricks elsewhere it's built on Apache Spark and the open Delta Lake format, combining cheap lake storage (ADLS) with warehouse-grade reliability (ACID on files). One platform spans data engineering (Spark ETL), SQL analytics (Databricks SQL), and ML/AI with notebooks, jobs and Unity Catalog governance. Its first-party status — native Azure portal experience, networking and identity — is what distinguishes it from the AWS/GCP deployments.

inPractice.narrative: Raw data lands in ADLS. Azure Databricks runs Spark to transform it into Delta tables (bronze/silver/gold) in the lake with ACID guarantees. Analysts query gold tables via Databricks SQL or connect Power BI directly; data scientists train models with MLflow; Unity Catalog and Entra ID govern access. Because it's first-party, identity and networking are native Azure. One platform carries data from raw lake files to BI and ML on Azure.

coreConcepts.detail: Provisioned and billed through Azure, with native Entra ID (Azure AD) auth, VNet injection, and tight ADLS/Synapse/Power BI integration — a smoother Azure experience than third-party deployments.
Warehouse-grade ACID, schema and time travel on open Parquet files in ADLS — one copy of data for ETL, ML and SQL.
Managed, auto-scaling Spark clusters (spot-capable) with the Photon engine for fast SQL/DataFrame workloads; serverless options remove cluster management.
SQL warehouses and dashboards over lakehouse tables; Power BI connects directly for downstream BI.
Centralised governance — catalog, lineage and fine-grained access — across workspaces, integrated with Azure identity.
Collaborative notebooks and MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry and deployment on one platform.

whenToUse: A unified lakehouse for ETL, SQL analytics and ML on Azure.
Large-scale Spark data engineering with reliable Delta tables.
Microsoft-stack teams wanting native Entra ID, ADLS and Power BI integration.
Collaborative data science with MLflow and notebooks.
An alternative/complement to Synapse Spark with the full Databricks platform.
whenNotToUse: Simple visual ETL/orchestration — Data Factory may be lighter.
Pure SQL-over-lake exploration only — Synapse serverless SQL is simpler.
Small workloads that don't justify the platform cost/complexity.
Teams wanting only Microsoft-native tooling with no third-party engine.

keyFacts.label: Engines

keyFacts.value: Unity Catalog integrated with Azure identity.

keyFacts.label: Billing
keyFacts.value: DBUs via Azure + Azure VM/storage underneath.

pricingShape: Azure Databricks bills in DBUs (by workload type and tier) through your Azure invoice, on top of the underlying Azure VM compute and ADLS storage. Two cost layers as on other clouds — Azure infrastructure plus the DBU premium — but it's all on one Azure bill. Levers: job clusters over all-purpose for scheduled work, auto-terminate idle clusters, spot VMs and Photon/serverless for efficiency, right-sizing, and Azure reservations for steady compute. Idle interactive clusters burning both VMs and DBUs remain the classic waste.
gotchas: Idle all-purpose clusters bill both DBUs and Azure VMs — set auto-termination.
Two cost layers (DBUs + Azure infra) make spend easy to underestimate.
Use job clusters for scheduled pipelines, not interactive clusters.
It overlaps with Synapse Spark — decide the boundary to avoid duplicated estates.
Delta still needs OPTIMIZE/VACUUM and small-file management for performance/cost.
